title: Use the bare artifact name as a contract schema's $id

values: contract schema (any, including schemas with a missing, prefixed or versioned $id, or a missing version field)
facts.note: Contract schemas and wagon manifests can be recognised by path/kind; the invariant applies to the whole schema, not only to edited fields.
Fires whenever a contract schema or wagon produce/consume entry is authored, edited or reviewed in a plan.
Covers both the schema $id/version and the contract: reference in wagon produce/consume entries.

values: version field added, changed or missing
produce/consume contract reference added or edited
facts.note: Needs a diff/content observer that extracts $id, version and contract: reference values from schemas and manifests.
Plan/wagon tasks mentioning contract schemas, their identity, versions or references.

fires: A planner writes a new contract schema and sets its $id.
A planner bumps a contract's version and is tempted to put the version into $id.
A planner edits any part of an existing contract schema whose $id is prefixed, versioned or missing, or which lacks a separate version field.
A planner adds or edits a wagon produce/consume entry that references a contract.
doesNotFire: Documents that are neither contract schemas nor wagon manifests (e.g. prose docs, plans without contract references).
Wagon manifest edits that do not touch produce/consume contract references.

given: You are planning, authoring or editing a contract schema, or a wagon produce/consume entry that references one.
when: The schema's $id is set, changed or present, or a reference to the contract is written.
then: Set the contract schema's $id to the clean artifact name {theme}:{resource}[.{category}] — no 'urn:contract:' prefix and no version suffix.
prefer: Required: record the contract's version in a separate top-level version field, never inside $id.
Write the wagon produce/consume reference as contract:{artifact_name}, using the same artifact name as the $id.
Keep $id stable across versions; express a new version through the separate version field.
avoid: Adding a version suffix to $id (e.g. ...:v1); it breaks identity stability across versions.
why: Keeping the version out of $id means the artifact keeps the same identity across versions, so $id and the contract: reference always point to one stable artifact.
evidence: Each contract schema's $id matches {theme}:{resource}[.{category}] with no 'urn:contract:' prefix and no version segment.
Each contract schema has a separate top-level version field.
Wagon produce/consume references have the form contract:{artifact_name}, and artifact_name equals the referenced schema's $id.
verifier_detail: Term id_field = 'the $id of a contract schema.' Values: id_pattern '{theme}:{resource}[.{category}]'; urn_reference 'contract:{artifact_name}'; version 'separate top-level field'.
Counter-example from source: mechanic:timebank.exhausted:v1 (version in $id breaks identity stability). Flag any trailing ':v<N>' or similar version segment in $id.
Flag contract schemas lacking a separate top-level version field.

splitSuggestion.then: Record every contract schema's version in a separate top-level version field so artifact identity stays stable across versions.
Reference contracts in wagon produce/consume entries as contract:{artifact_name}, where artifact_name equals the schema's $id.

additions.text: The source bundles three obligations: clean $id (kept in then), separate top-level version field (kept as a mandatory 'Required:' prefer[0] and evidence[1]), and contract:{artifact_name} references (prefer[1], evidence[2]). Separate conventions planner.artifact-naming.schema-version-field and planner.artifact-naming.contract-urn-reference should exist.
additions.justification: One-obligation rule for then; mandatory force of the version-field requirement is preserved via prefer[0], evidence[1] and verifier_detail[4].
